topic: Who already sells Batch Zero / large-load verification RFI support in ERCOT? (crowding check, as of 21 Nov 2026)

findings.claim: In 12 live searches I found no firm that markets the specific service: assembling the Batch Zero verification RFI evidence package and running a desk that answers within the 10 business days. The count found is zero. That is not proof that nobody offers it.
findings.detail: Searches using practitioner terms ('Batch Zero' verification RFI response help, attestation consultant, long-lead equipment evidence package, plus named engineering firms and law firms) returned ERCOT documents, law-firm alerts, intel/explainer sites and engineering-modelling pages. None advertised RFI evidence assembly, exhibit-list preparation, notarisation coordination or a fixed-turnaround response service. The search tool's own summary of the most targeted query said it 'found no consultants, advisory firms, or "we help" offers for Batch Zero verification RFI responses.' Caveats (INFERRED): some firms may do this work quietly inside existing owner's-engineer or legal engagements without advertising it, and searches cannot see LinkedIn posts, gated pages or what firms say directly to clients.

findings.claim: Keentel Engineering markets Batch Zero work most actively among the engineering firms found. Its offer is technical studies and models, not verification RFI responses.
findings.detail: SOURCED (vendor marketing, via search snippets): Keentel runs several Batch Zero pages: a Batch Zero guide on large-load and ride-through rules, a 'Batch Zero ERCOT Compliance & Large Load Guide', a PCLR/Batch Zero guide and a POI interconnection page for data centres. The services it lists are applicability and grandfathering assessments, PERC1 model development and conversion, hardware-benchmarked PSCAD converter validation, and ride-through and stability studies. None of these pages surfaced any verification RFI or evidence-package offer. Firm size: not established. The search summary also flagged that the page dates look inconsistent.

findings.claim: EPE Consulting markets 'Batch Zero readiness reviews' alongside PERC1 model updates and DWG survey revisions. This is the closest named offer to readiness work, but it centres on models and data, not RFI documents.
findings.detail: SOURCED (vendor news pages, via search snippet): EPE has published on PGRR145 filing and ERCOT Board approval of Batch Zero, and lists PERC1 model updates, DWG Large Load Data Survey revisions and Batch Zero readiness reviews. I found no evidence that the readiness review covers verification RFI items such as long-lead equipment POs and delivery schedules, site control, or attestations, or that EPE offers a 10-day response service. A targeted search for EPE plus readiness review returned nothing beyond this. Size: not established.

findings.claim: Smaller Texas grid specialists, Zero Emission Grid (ZEG) and NFM Consulting, are in the large-load space. Neither showed a verification RFI offer.
findings.detail: SOURCED: ZEG says it provides engineering and consulting to help generation, storage and large-load developers evaluate grid constraints. It filed PGRR145 comments and publishes detailed summaries of ERCOT Batch Zero and LLWG meetings, including the 10 Dec 2026 eligibility-report milestone. NFM Consulting (San Antonio, in ERCOT markets since 2017) markets help for large loads complying with Texas SB 6 rules on interconnection, curtailment and ride-through. A targeted search pairing both with 'verification RFI support' found no matching service page. Size: not established for either.

findings.claim: Among the large engineering firms, only Burns & McDonnell's 1898 & Co showed public Batch Zero material, and it is a technical white paper, not a verification service. Black & Veatch, POWER Engineers, Quanta, Sargent & Lundy and ENGIE Impact did not surface at all.
findings.detail: SOURCED: 1898 & Co published 'Dynamic Limits of Net Zero Large Load Interconnection in ERCOT's Batch Zero Framework', which covers co-located generation and storage. A search naming Black & Veatch and POWER Engineers found nothing tying them to Batch Zero advisory work. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether these firms do verification documentation for existing data-centre clients. INFERRED: large owner's-engineer and EPC firms already hold procurement records (POs, delivery schedules, one-lines, site plans) for their own clients. That makes them likely to absorb this work for their own clients rather than sell it as a standalone service.

findings.claim: At least 9 law firms publish Batch Zero alerts, and Baker Botts and Gibson Dunn cover the verification and audit process specifically. These alerts market legal advice (classification, disputes, attestation exposure), not a document-assembly desk. None of the firms the brief named (Jackson Walker, Husch Blackwell, V&E, Bracewell, Norton Rose, Winston & Strawn) appeared.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Baker Botts published 'Texas Large Load Interconnection Update: ERCOT Batch Zero Pause and Verification Process' (Aug 2026) and 'ERCOT Batch Zero: Next Steps' (Sept 2026). The second advises projects to confirm their 3 Sep conditional classifications and preserve dispute rights, and notes PG 9.1(8) lets ERCOT request supporting documentation and verify site readiness through 9 Apr 2027. Gibson Dunn analysed the Governor's 3 Aug audit directive: non-compliant projects 'must be denied' interconnection. Other firms with Batch Zero alerts: Foley, Willkie, Seyfarth, Sheppard Mullin, Akin Gump, S. Deatherage Law, and the bwenergylaw.com blog. There is also a Mondaq syndication. INFERRED: these firms will review and sign off on notarised attestations given the false-information risk, but none advertises preparing evidence packages.

findings.claim: A cluster of intel and explainer sites already covers the verification RFIs: Cutrer Labs, Hyperscape Digital, LoadAtlas, JD Key, metaprompt.ai and The Texas Dispatch. None was shown to sell response services.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Cutrer Labs published 'ERCOT starts sending Batch Zero verification requests, with notarized attestations due in 10 business days'. Hyperscape Digital has a Batch Zero scorecard explainer. LoadAtlas has an ERCOT large-load process page. JD Key (James Dickey) published 'Batch Zero: what it takes to keep your Texas power allocation' plus a newsletter; the article notes that developers and TSPs stay responsible for their own data, exhibits and sworn attestations. metaprompt.ai has a November 2026 audit timeline. The Texas Dispatch ran 'ERCOT Demands Sworn Data Center Proof or Loss of Place'. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any of these sell services. INFERRED: they show the topic is well covered as content, so information alone will not differentiate a new entrant.

findings.claim: The RFI work is heavy and split across three parties, and ERCOT itself says long-lead equipment evidence is the most common failure point. That is the gap a specialist package would fill.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Each of the ILLE (the large-load developer), the interconnecting TSP and, where applicable, the DSP must give a notarised attestation and a BZ Verification RFI Exhibit List naming every document relied on. Only the TSP submits in RIOO (ERCOT's online portal), and the TSP can get one 5-business-day extension by emailing LargeLoadVerification@ercot.com. ERCOT's reference question sets are long: 48 pages for one pathway and 32 for the studied-load pathway, with guides for four eligibility pathways in all. ERCOT's Senate briefing lists the supporting evidence as long-lead equipment POs, real-estate agreements, land-use approvals and end-user agreements. ERCOT's PUCT filing names 'inability to establish long-lead time equipment ordered and will be delivered before energization' as a common issue. ERCOT can also issue supplemental requests. A separate State and Community Impact RFI, also filed by the TSP/DSP in RIOO, was due 12 Oct 2026.

findings.claim: Timing: the first wave of RFIs, issued from 9 Sep 2026, is almost certainly past its deadlines. The remaining demand is supplemental RFIs, the 10 Dec verification report and what follows it, verification through 9 Apr 2027, and Batch 1 from Summer 2027.
findings.detail: SOURCED: ERCOT began issuing verification RFIs on 9 Sep 2026 and must file its Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report by 10 Dec 2026. Energisation approvals for new large-load data centres and crypto facilities are paused until verification ends. Baker Botts cites PG 9.1(8), which lets ERCOT request documentation and verify site readiness through 9 Apr 2027, the same date the Batch Zero Interconnection Study report is due. ERCOT says Batch 1 applications open in Summer 2027. INFERRED: 10 business days from 9 Sep is about 23 Sep, or about 30 Sep with the extension, so most first-round responses are already in. A 10-day response desk launched now would mainly serve supplemental requests, appeals of exclusions, late-issued RFIs and Batch 1 preparation.

findings.claim: Demand is large in gigawatts, but the number of projects and RFIs is not established.
findings.detail: SOURCED: A PUCT filing (Project 59142) reports 191.8 GW in Batch Zero (base plus studied load) and 302.2 GW not included. ERCOT has cited more than 438,000 MW of large-load requests, about 89% from data centres. JD Key reports ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas putting about 205 GW as potentially eligible and about 65 GW on a clearer five-year path, and expects projects that cannot show security, site control or equipment orders to drop out. NOT ESTABLISHED: the count of projects or RFIs issued, how many TSPs are involved, response and exclusion rates, and any market price for RFI support. None of this surfaced in these searches.

bottom_line: Nobody visibly sells the exact service yet, but it is a niche next to a crowded field, and the urgent first-round window has probably closed. I found zero firms marketing a verification RFI evidence package with a 10-day response desk. Keentel, EPE Consulting, ZEG and NFM sell technical Batch Zero work: models, ride-through studies and readiness reviews. 1898 & Co publishes thought leadership. At least nine law firms (Baker Botts, Gibson Dunn, Foley, Willkie, Seyfarth, Sheppard Mullin, Akin Gump and others) market advice on classification, disputes and attestations. Intel sites (Cutrer Labs, Hyperscape, LoadAtlas, JD Key) already explain the RFIs for free. The gap is plausible because the work is document-heavy and split across three parties: notarised ILLE/TSP/DSP attestations, an exhibit list, and question sets of 32 to 48 pages. ERCOT itself names long-lead equipment proof as the most common failure, and law firms and modelling engineers do not naturally assemble POs, delivery schedules and labelled one-lines. Three cautions (INFERRED): (1) RFIs went out from 9 Sep 2026 with 10+5-day deadlines, so first-round demand is mostly spent. Remaining demand is supplemental RFIs, exclusions and appeals around the 10 Dec report, verification through 9 Apr 2027, and Batch 1 preparation from Summer 2027. A firm should therefore sell this as readiness: a standing evidence file kept current before the RFI arrives, more than as an emergency desk. (2) Owner's engineers and law firms can easily add this for their existing clients, so differentiation needs speed, templates mapped to the LLE-1 to LLE-8 items, and coordination with TSPs. TSPs are also a buyer, because they carry the filing obligation. (3) Project counts, prices and competitor sizes are not established, so a few direct conversations with TSPs and developers should test demand before investing.

topic: Market size, channel and state of play for ERCOT Batch Zero verification (as of 21 Nov 2026)

findings.claim: ERCOT began issuing Batch Zero Verification RFIs on 9 Sep 2026 and sent them to the ILLEs through their TSPs or DSPs. An early PUCT filing counts one RFI for each of 231 Large Load projects.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Market notice M-A090926-01 (9 Sep 2026) says RFIs went to 'a majority' of ILLEs with a conditionally included Large Load. Responses are due within 10 Business Days, with at most a 5-Business-Day extension. An incomplete or late response 'will result in the Large Load being excluded'. ERCOT continued sending RFIs to the remaining loads through the end of September. Notice M-C092126-01 posted Question Reference Guides for the four eligibility pathways that received an RFI. Questions go to LargeLoadVerification@ercot.com. Jeff Billo's September Board deck says the RFIs go to ILLEs 'through their TDSPs'. Trade press (Cutrer Labs) reports that the RFIs require notarized attestations. SOURCED-WEAK: the figure of one RFI for each of 231 projects comes from a search summary of the 11 Sep PUCT Docket 59142 filing. I could not open the filing to confirm it. INFERRED: the 10+5 Business Day window means first-round responses were due between about 23 Sep and late Oct 2026, so that initial response window has already closed. Not established: a final count of all verification RFIs issued, including follow-up or deficiency RFIs.

findings.claim: The population is about 362 conditionally included large loads, totalling about 194 GW (66.4 GW base and 127.9 GW studied). Another 373 projects totalling 302.2 GW were excluded.
findings.detail: SOURCED-WEAK, from secondary reporting of ERCOT's 3 Sep 2026 provisional classifications. Base load: 204 projects, 66.4 GW. Studied load: 158 projects, 127.9 GW. One source gives 125.4 GW for the studied tier, so the figures do not fully agree. Excluded load: 373 projects, 302.2 GW. ERCOT says these classifications are not final and depend on the eligibility verification and audit. Billo's September deck also says ERCOT moved some projects submitted as base load into the studied category. It also records 41 good-cause exception requests received on 23 Jul 2026, and that ERCOT will not pursue every one. INFERRED: the directly addressable set for verification-RFI support is a few hundred projects, roughly 360 conditional loads plus about 41 good-cause exception requests. It is a niche of high-value accounts, not a mass market.

findings.claim: In a separate RFI stream, ERCOT sent the Data Center State and Community Impact RFI to 465 loads. 433 of them (93%) responded, covering about 177 GW (about 97% of the requested capacity).
findings.detail: SOURCED-WEAK: the figures come from a search summary of ERCOT's 4 Nov 2026 filing in PUCT Docket 59142 (item 78). The summary text was slightly garbled ('-177 GW (-97%)'), and I could not open the PDF. This is the Community Impact Audit RFI, which covers computational loads of 25 MW and above. It is not the Batch Zero eligibility verification RFI. Large Computational Loads of 75 MW or more face both audits (Baker Botts). INFERRED: response rates are high, and the 32 loads that did not respond are the most visible candidates for removal. A second RFI regime with its own documentation demands shows that ILLEs and TSPs face a stacked compliance workload.

findings.claim: I found no public report of loads removed from Batch Zero or failing verification. Final inclusion and exclusion will come in ERCOT's Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report, due 10 Dec 2026; one source says 3 Dec.
findings.detail: NOT ESTABLISHED: in 12 searches I found no named or counted removals. SOURCED: ERCOT has said that a materially false attestation, failure to respond, or failure to meet the verification requirements leads to exclusion or ineligibility (market notice; Gibson Dunn; The Leveraged Years). ERCOT told its Board it will file the report with the PUCT by 10 Dec 2026. One newer article gives 3 Dec, so the date is contested. The deadline for Batch Zero study results, 9 Apr 2027, remains unchanged. SOURCED-WEAK, single unverified source: ERCOT reviewed 290 dynamic models and about 18% were acceptable on first review. If that is right, many projects face deficiency-cure work as well as attestation verification.

findings.claim: The latest official ERCOT large-load queue total I found is 474.7 GW through 2033, as of June 2026, with about 90% data centres. I found no October or November 2026 total.
findings.detail: SOURCED: ERCOT gave the Texas Senate on 29 Jul 2026 a figure of 474.7 GW as of June 2026, with data centres at about 90%. Utility Dive and others repeat it. Earlier ERCOT figures were about 410 GW (about 87% data centres) as of 26 Mar 2026, about 438 GW at the PUCT's 18 Jun 2026 Batch Zero approval, and about 226 GW in Nov 2025. ercotqueue.com shows an undated 466 GW. ERCOT has paused energization approvals for data-centre and crypto loads of 75 MW or more until verification is complete. Loads of 25-75 MW are outside the pause. INFERRED: only about 194 GW of the roughly 475 GW queue (about 40%) is conditionally in Batch Zero. Most of the queue is waiting for a later batch, and those projects will face similar documentation tests.

findings.claim: Oncor is the dominant TSP channel. At 30 Sep 2026 it held 795 active transmission large-load requests, about 293 GW of them data centres. About 45 GW of its load is conditionally in Batch Zero.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Oncor's Q3 2026 results and trade coverage report 795 active transmission large commercial and industrial requests at 30 Sep 2026. About 293 GW are data centres, up from 282 GW at 30 Jun and about 271 GW at 31 Mar. Another roughly 19 GW is other industrial load, including 4 GW of crypto. ERCOT has conditionally classified about 24 GW of Oncor load as base load (10 GW already energized) and 21 GW as studied load. INFERRED: Oncor's roughly 45 GW is about 23% of the roughly 194 GW conditionally included. Its 795 requests suggest heavy TSP-side workload for the 10-Business-Day RFI submissions. Oncor's queue basis (requests per TSP) is not directly comparable to ERCOT's 474.7 GW total. Not established: whether Oncor has published its own process for handling Batch Zero RFIs, or whether it is visibly overloaded.

findings.claim: CenterPoint submitted more than 17 GW to Batch Zero and expects about 14 GW to qualify. AEP Texas reported 36 GW of SB6-compliant, LOA-backed large loads. I found no figures for TNMP, LCRA TSC, CPS Energy, Austin Energy or co-ops.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Utility Dive reports that CenterPoint, on its Q2 2026 earnings call, said it had submitted more than 17 GW of large-load projects to Batch Zero and expected 14 GW to be eligible. CenterPoint separately cites about 8 GW of incremental Houston data-centre load by 2029. AEP Texas reported 36 GW of SB6-compliant large loads backed by letters of agreement in Feb 2026. I found no Q3 update. NOT ESTABLISHED: large-load request volumes, or published Batch Zero RFI processes, for TNMP, LCRA TSC, CPS Energy, Austin Energy, Brazos or other co-ops and munis. INFERRED: Oncor, CenterPoint and AEP Texas together likely account for most Batch Zero capacity. That would make channel or partnership sales concentrated among three or four TSPs.

findings.claim: The PUCT adopted the SB 6 large-load interconnection rule (16 TAC §25.194, Project 58481) in September 2026, effective about 8 Oct 2026. It dropped the proposed $50,000/MW non-refundable fee in favour of a flat $100,000 study fee.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Utility Dive and others report adoption of a 'softened' rule around 18 Sep 2026; one source says 20 Sep. The final rule removes the March draft's non-refundable $50k/MW interconnection fee and sets a flat $100k study fee. One aggregator headline mentions '$50,000 per MW of security', which I could not confirm. SB 6 transmission cost-allocation rules are due by 31 Dec 2026, and more rulemakings continue under Project 58317. I found no further PUCT large-load rule adopted in November 2026. INFERRED: a lower entry cost may keep speculative projects in the queue, which keeps verification scrutiny on documentation, including long-lead-equipment purchase orders, high in later batches.

findings.claim: Political shift: Gina Hinojosa won the 3 Nov 2026 Texas governor's race. She has pledged to continue halting new data-centre approvals until the Legislature acts, and she takes office 19 Jan 2027.
findings.detail: SOURCED-WEAK, from search summaries of DCD and Baxtel; I did not open the articles. Hinojosa, now governor-elect, is reported to back a moratorium on new data-centre approvals lasting until lawmakers pass protections, possibly through a special session. Before the election she urged Abbott to pause new data centres until lawmakers act (Fox 4). The 90th Legislature convenes in January 2027. One expert told E&E News he would be surprised if 2027 bills applied to Batch Zero projects. Abbott's 3 Aug 2026 directive remains the basis for the current pause and audit. INFERRED: the December verification report lands in a lame-duck period. Projects that clear verification may still face a hold on approvals under the new governor. The value of airtight, defensible documentation therefore rises, but the timeline to energization and Batch Zero study completion becomes less certain.

findings.claim: The 19 Nov 2026 Large Load Working Group meeting took place, but I found no agenda, materials or outcomes. The next LLWG meeting is 17 Dec 2026.
findings.detail: SOURCED: the ERCOT calendar lists the LLWG meeting on 19 Nov 2026 at 9:30 AM, ERCOT Austin (8000 Metropolis, Bldg E) and Webex, with the next meeting on 17 Dec 2026. NOT ESTABLISHED: anything discussed on 19 Nov, such as verification statistics, PGRR145 or PGRR144 follow-ups, or Batch One design. Billo's September Board deck also noted 6 large-load projects expected for the August QSA and 17 potentially eligible for the November QSA. INFERRED: the 17 Dec LLWG, the 10 Dec (or 3 Dec) verification report and the December Board meeting are the next points where counts of removals and RFIs should appear.

bottom_line:
The market for answering ERCOT's first-round Batch Zero verification requests (RFIs) is small and has mostly passed already. The opportunity now is in the cleanup that follows, the next batch, and selling through the utilities that submit on developers' behalf.

1. **Size.** About 362 projects totalling about 194 GW were conditionally let into Batch Zero (sourced, from secondary reports). One early filing counts 231 projects receiving RFIs. ERCOT sent most RFIs in September with a 10+5 Business Day clock, so most first-round answers were due between late September and late October. That means a few hundred high-value accounts, most of which have already responded. A separate community-impact survey drew answers from 93% of 465 loads (sourced-weak).

2. **What comes next.** The near-term work is:
   - fixing deficiencies ERCOT flags;
   - challenging or curing results after ERCOT's verification report, due 10 Dec (or 3 Dec);
   - redoing dynamic models. One unverified source says only about 18% passed on first review.
   - documenting long-lead equipment (purchase orders, delivery dates) for loads that stay in, ahead of the 9 Apr 2027 study-results deadline.

   I found no reported removals yet. Expect the first exclusions in December.

3. **The bigger pool.** 373 projects totalling 302 GW were excluded from Batch Zero, and most of the roughly 475 GW queue (June 2026, about 90% data centres) has to pass similar documentation tests in later batches. That is the larger, recurring market (inferred).

4. **Channel.** The duty to submit sits with the transmission or distribution utility, and it is concentrated:
   - Oncor has 795 large-load requests, about 293 GW of data centres, and about 45 GW conditionally in Batch Zero.
   - CenterPoint submitted 17 GW and expects 14 GW to qualify.
   - AEP Texas reported 36 GW of qualifying large loads.

   Partnering with these three, or with developers using them, reaches most of the capacity. I found no data on TNMP, LCRA, CPS Energy, Austin Energy or the co-ops, so that remains not established.

5. **Demand risk.** Governor-elect Hinojosa (sourced-weak) takes office 19 Jan 2027 and has pledged to keep halting new data-centre approvals until the Legislature acts. Energization stays paused for loads of 75 MW and up. This raises the cost of a false or incomplete filing, which supports demand for documentation rigour. It also stretches how long developers wait for any payoff, which may make them cautious about spending.

**Positioning.** Sell readiness and cure work as a retainer through Q1 2027, not as one-off RFI responses. Aim first at Oncor- and CenterPoint-area developers and at the excluded or next-batch pipeline. Watch three things before committing heavily: the December verification report, the 17 Dec LLWG meeting, and the new governor's first actions.

topic: Pricing and the adjacent revenue: NOGRR282 ride-through, SB 6 / PUCT rules, and whether verification-type work recurs after ERCOT Batch Zero

findings.claim: The only published, regulator-set price for large-load interconnection in ERCOT is the PUCT's flat $100,000 study fee plus $50,000 per MW of financial security. The proposed non-refundable $50,000/MW interconnection fee was dropped.
findings.detail: SOURCED: 16 TAC §25.194 (Project 58481) was adopted at the PUCT open meeting on 18 Sep 2026 (one source says 20 Sep) and took effect 8 Oct 2026. The adoption order text says a large load customer pays a $100,000 study fee for ERCOT's study costs, and any unused amount is refunded within 60 days after the study ends. Secondary sources, plus the order excerpt, report security of $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand. Worked example from one source: a 500 MW campus posts $25M of security plus the $100k fee. The fee is flat, not tiered by size, and the PUCT said it may update it as cost data comes in. The rule applies to new single-site loads of 75 MW or more and certain expansions. It also requires the customer to tell the interconnecting TSP/DSP whether it plans to register as a Controllable Load Resource. Sources disagree on when the security is refundable, so check the rule text. NOT ESTABLISHED: any separate per-utility study charge from Oncor or CenterPoint. For context only, Oncor reported 650 active large C&I interconnection requests at the end of 2025.

findings.claim: No published consultant day rates or engagement sizes for ERCOT large-load interconnection or compliance work could be found. Only indirect price markers exist.
findings.detail: NOT ESTABLISHED: consultant hourly or day rates, retainer sizes, or fixed fees for Batch Zero, NOGRR282 or SB 6 compliance work. No source in 12 searches published one. SOURCED PROXIES ONLY, none of them consultant billing rates: (a) AEP Ohio publishes one-time load-study fees of $10k (25 to under 50 MW), $50k (50 to under 100 MW) and $100k (100 MW and up), per a secondary cost guide. (b) The same guide puts ISO study deposits at $50k to $640k per stage. (c) A Siemens 'Senior Power Systems Consultant - PSCAD' posting lists a salary of $83,966 to $143,942. That is employee pay, not a billing rate. Also NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the PUCT or ERCOT hired an outside firm for the data-center audit, or at what contract value. INFERRED: consulting fees are probably small next to the capital a client has at risk ($25M of security on a 500 MW project), which argues for pricing by value rather than by day. That is reasoning, not a market price.

findings.claim: NOGRR282 (with NPRR1308) is in force from 1 Aug 2026. It applies to Large Electronic or Computational Loads: Large Loads of 75 MW or more where at least 50% of site demand is computational (data centers, crypto mining).
findings.detail: SOURCED: The ERCOT Board adopted NOGRR282 and NPRR1308 on 2 Jun 2026, the PUCT approved both at its 9 Jul 2026 open meeting, and the effective date is 1 Aug 2026. NPRR1308 defines a Large Electronic Load as a Large Load (>75 MW) where 50% or more of site demand is computational. NOGRR282 adds frequency and voltage ride-through sections to the Nodal Operating Guides (sources differ on the section numbers). Sources use 'LEL' and 'LCL' for the same category.

findings.claim: NOGRR282 obligations are phased. Compliance is a condition of energization for new LELs, older loads get a limited exemption, and a stricter tier applies to LELs energized after 1 Jan 2028.
findings.detail: SOURCED (ERCOT presentation and comments, plus consultants): ERCOT proposed a limited exemption for LELs approved to energize on or before 14 Nov 2025, or that met certain significant development milestones by that date. Other loads must meet the requirements as a condition of energization. ERCOT's 11 May 2026 comments asked that any surviving cooling-load exemption end no later than 30 Jun 2027. That is ERCOT's position in the record and is not confirmed as final text. EPE Consulting reports additional, stricter voltage-dip performance requirements for LELs energized after 1 Jan 2028. One consultant's timeline labels 14 Nov 2025 as 'initial compliance', but that is the date the request was submitted, so treat consultant dates with caution. NOT ESTABLISHED: a deadline for submitting PSCAD/EMT models, or a deadline for retrofitting loads that are already energized.

findings.claim: NOGRR282 needs engineering evidence: ride-through performance by design, protection-setting limits, and root-cause reports after events. That is power-systems engineering work, not document assembly.
findings.detail: SOURCED (secondary summaries, not checked against the final rule text): Voltage ride-through runs from 2 s at 0.85 pu down to 150 ms below 0.35 pu. The load must return to 90% of its pre-disturbance consumption within 2 s, inrush is capped at 150% at the point of interconnection, and the load must withstand six sags in 90 s. Protection may not trip or transfer solely on a count of sags or swells. Frequency ride-through requires continuous operation in a central band (one source says 58.8 to 61.2 Hz; others differ). Ride-through is not required while the load is in under-frequency load shedding or providing an Ancillary Service. If ERCOT finds a load failed to ride through, the customer must report the root cause within 90 days of ERCOT's request. That is a recurring, event-driven obligation. INFERRED: showing compliance calls for EMT/PSCAD modelling, UPS, cooling and protection coordination, and post-event forensics, which a document-verification firm would need engineers to deliver.

findings.claim: Named firms already publish ride-through and large-load compliance material on their own service sites, and large law firms cover the SB 6 and Batch Zero regulatory side.
findings.detail: SOURCED (each firm has published content on the topic; their pricing is NOT ESTABLISHED). Engineering and consulting: Keentel Engineering (ERCOT ride-through, POI interconnection and NERC data-center pages), Zero Emission Grid, 3DFS, Battalion Energy, EPE Consulting, RMS Energy, NFM Consulting, gr1d, Applied Technical Services (Texas data center compliance). On the NERC side: ScottMadden and Ampyx Cyber. Law firms publishing on SB 6 and the Batch Zero pause or verification: Baker Botts, Akin Gump, Holland & Knight, Gibson Dunn, Greenberg Traurig, White & Case, Troutman Pepper Locke, Seyfarth, Sidley and Willkie. INFERRED: ride-through and NERC work is already contested by engineering firms, and the legal and regulatory layer by law firms. The gap a Batch Zero firm could hold is running the evidence and RFI file between the client, the TSP and these specialists.

findings.claim: SB 6 puts ongoing operating obligations on large loads, mainly curtailment readiness. Further rulemakings are still open.
findings.detail: SOURCED: Transmission-voltage customers that interconnect after 31 Dec 2025 must accept a protocol allowing their load to be curtailed during firm load shed, with exceptions for certain critical loads. For co-located, net-metered loads under 16 TAC §25.205 (Project 58479, reportedly adopted 26 Mar 2026), the first order (Docket 59220) reportedly requires full-campus curtailment within 30 minutes of an ERCOT emergency instruction. Under 16 TAC §25.370 (Project 58480, forecasting), the 2026 RTP load forecast excluded load data submitted after, or still incomplete at, 1 Apr 2026. After 2026, only loads with an executed interconnection agreement meeting Project 58481 will be counted. Still open: Project 58482 (large-load demand reduction or reliability service) was 'in development' as of Sep 2026. The PUCT staff expected to propose a standard interconnection agreement rule in Oct 2026. NOT ESTABLISHED: final SB 6 backup-generation disclosure terms or any periodic reporting schedule.

findings.claim: Batch Zero is paused under a governor-ordered audit. ERCOT expects to finish around 10 Dec 2026, and energization approvals for loads of 75 MW or more are on hold until then.
findings.detail: SOURCED: On 3 Aug 2026 Gov. Abbott directed the PUCT and ERCOT to audit data centers in the interconnection process; projects that fail must be denied connection. ERCOT missed the 7 Aug deadline for Batch Zero classification notices and paused classification and study work. It split the work into a Batch Zero eligibility audit and a community-impact audit covering 247 large (75 MW and up) and 214 medium (25 to 75 MW) data centers. On 21 Sep 2026 Abbott froze TCEQ permits for data centers until the audit finishes. ERCOT halted approvals to energize loads of 75 MW or more. ERCOT expects to finish the audit on or around 10 Dec 2026 (per Houston Public Media). ERCOT was tracking about 410 GW of large-load requests in April 2026, about 87% of them data centers; Utility Dive cites about 474 GW. SOURCED-WEAK, UNVERIFIED: one garbled MLQ.ai piece says an incoming governor would keep approvals frozen until the Legislature acts. Do not rely on it.

findings.claim: The largest source of durable, recurring compliance work is federal. FERC ordered NERC to file computational-load reliability standards and registration criteria by 31 Dec 2026, and registration is expected in 2027.
findings.detail: SOURCED: FERC's 16 Jul 2026 order in Docket RD26-7-000 directs NERC to file new or modified standards, plus Rules of Procedure and registry criteria for computational load entities, by 31 Dec 2026. A further informational filing on the work plan is due 1 Mar 2027. Nothing binds data centers until FERC approves; one law-firm analysis expects registration in 2027. NERC issued a Level 3 alert on computational loads on 4 May 2026, with essential actions on modelling, instrumentation and ride-through. SOURCED-WEAK (blogs or vendors, unconfirmed against NERC): NERC's 19 Aug 2026 draft splits registration into Computational Load Owner and Operator, at 50 MW and 100 kV. NERC reportedly adopted CLO-001-1 through CLO-003-1 on 26 Oct 2026. INFERRED: NERC registration would bring standing compliance programs (evidence retention, periodic audits or self-certification) at a lower threshold than ERCOT's 75 MW.

findings.claim: Recurrence check: Batch Zero verification and the 25.194 study/security steps are one-off for each project. The obligations that recur are ride-through event reporting, curtailment readiness, annual forecast data and, from about 2027, NERC registration.
findings.detail: INFERRED, from the sourced items above. One-off per project: Batch Zero RFI responses (10 Business Days each, with a 5-day extension), the $100k study fee and $50k/MW security, the CLR disclosure, and NOGRR282 compliance shown at energization. Recurring or event-driven: NOGRR282 root-cause reports within 90 days after a failed ride-through; curtailment readiness under SB 6 and the 30-minute net-metering order; annual RTP load-forecast data with hard cutoffs such as 1 Apr 2026; IA execution, which now decides whether a load is counted in the forecast; the stricter NOGRR282 tier after 1 Jan 2028; and NERC computational-load registration and standards from about 2027. Keentel (secondary) lists post-energization duties of forecasting, curtailment availability, disturbance data sharing and periodic model validation. NOT ESTABLISHED: any quarterly re-verification, a telemetry reporting schedule, or whether later ERCOT batches will reuse the same RFI verification design.

bottom_line:
A firm built only on Batch Zero verification RFIs is selling a one-off service, and it is currently frozen. The governor's audit has paused Batch Zero classification and study work and halted energization approvals for loads of 75 MW or more. ERCOT expects to finish around 10 Dec 2026, and political risk may extend that. There is durable follow-on work, but most of it is engineering and regulatory, not document assembly:
(1) NOGRR282 ride-through compliance is a condition of energization for every new 75 MW+ computational load. A stricter tier follows after 1 Jan 2028, and failed events trigger 90-day root-cause reports.
(2) SB 6 obligations: posting the 25.194 security, the CLR disclosure and executing the interconnection agreement (which now decides forecast inclusion), plus curtailment readiness. Projects 58482 and the standard interconnection agreement rule are still pending.
(3) The largest recurring stream is likely NERC computational-load registration from about 2027, possibly at 50 MW and 100 kV.
Engineering firms (Keentel, ZEG, EPE, Battalion, 3DFS, ScottMadden, Ampyx) and big law firms already cover these areas. A verification firm's defensible place is the evidence and RFI program office tying the client, the TSP and those specialists together. To sell ride-through or NERC work itself, it would need to hire engineers or partner with them.
On price, no market consultant rates were found. The only hard figures are the PUCT's $100k study fee and $50k/MW security ($25M for 500 MW). That suggests pricing by value at risk, but it does not give a market rate.
